title: Military Zone and Item Placement Handling
body:
This request accounts for re-creating the SimulationProposeMilitaryBase function with all of the original base-types now available (as per DOS and Mac).

When it comes to the Navy placement specifically, it now accounts for the selected view rotation.

The ItemPlacementCheck function has also been re-created and the specific "if" that prevented Military Zone populating cases has been commented out.

The original related hooks have been removed at this point.

Some attempted demystification has been performed as well.

When the time comes to merge, a squash is likely recommended.
author: af-az

comments.body: `GAMECALL_NOCONV` can be replaced by just a `GAMECALL` using `__stdcall` as the calling convention, similar to the `GAMECALL` for `ToolMenuUpdate`. The calling convention only really matters for functions with arguments so technically `__stdcall` and `__cdecl` are identical for a function without arguments.

Replaced as recommended.

Tested as well, nothing anomalous.

Flagged for review at this point.

title: Add in two defines for if they're not present by default.
body:
Both of the referenced defines have been added locally for if they're not present by default.

(There is still one case in vs2015 where the build will fail if _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS isn't set, but that doesn't crop up for vs2022 - it hasn't been included at this time)
author: af-az

comments.body:
Honestly it might be worth it to bump the build requirements up to VS2019 -- Kuroko's built-in documentation system requires C11 generics, which were added to VS2019 version 16.8 (_MSC_VER == 1928), so without turning on /std:c11 all the built-in help routines are dummied out.

I'll see if I can make it so that the default behaviour is to build with /std:c11 or /std:c17 but fall back to /std:c99 if the project file is loaded in VS2019 version 16.7 or older, and throw some additional preprocessor magic in the Kuroko headers to detect that.

That makes sense.

At the very least with the two defines added locally it did allow for the library to be built from vs2015 (aside from the as-noted '_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS' case there weren't any problems).

title: Center tool scrolling disabled except when the 'Alt' key is pressed down.
body:
The Left Mouse Button Down, Mouse First and MapToolMenuAction functions have been hooked and completely overriden.

I've placed this into draft mode for the time being due to how some of the game functions are currently called at the local level (pending clarification and then classification unless they end up with their current generic names).
author: af-az

comments.body: Reviewing the game functions that are defined at a local level, attempting to get them classified (or at least clarified) and cleaned up.

Quick note on the window messages that IDA generates: WM_MOUSEFIRST is actually supposed to be WM_MOUSEMOVE; both are defined to the 0x200, and WM_MOUSEMOVE is the "actual" message but since WM_MOUSEFIRST is alphabetically first, IDA uses that in the AFX_MSGMAP_ENTRY.

WM_MOUSEFIRST and WM_MOUSELAST are defines for the beginning and end of the mouse messages. I can't remember exactly what the purpose of them is, but they're more delimiters than actual intended message names. I think it dates back to the really early Windows API when having a mouse attached to the system wasn't actually necessarily a given.

Yep, this has now been accounted for.

One detail though; I'm not sure if there are any potential conflicting (or out-right incorrectly named function/variables) that are coming from the game, hopefully those that have been specified thus far are accurate (or at least close until further demystifying takes place).

That's pretty much all I've got ready at this point as far as variables go. If we have to rename stuff upon further discovery of what things do in the future, then that's fine. I'd rather have some reasonable names established now. For any future changes we can update sc2k_1996.h (and any future modding modules) later.

One thing I've noticed is that if you name a function in IDA "GetFooBarBazQuux" and then hit F5 again to re-run the decompilation, it'll name whatever associated local variable "FooBarBazQuux". I think our only current "rule" really as far as naming functions go is not to name anything that doesn't return a fixed pointer "GetDoodad" to a) make sure things aren't ambiguous and b) keep IDA happy.
Finished off the last of the local-level to global-header game-function adjustments, hopefully the chosen names are reasonably useful.
Let me know if you'd prefer a "squashed" commit under this circumstance and I'll re-issue the pull request.

Rad, thanks. I can do a squish and merge on my end. I've been trying to figure out some stuff regarding the scrollbars so I might fiddle with some names if anything matches what I've poked at but other than that it looks good to go.

title: Program Portability - All settings stored in ini file
body:
I've placed this pull request in "draft" mode for now since there's still one area I'm undecided about, I suppose it depends on whether it matters (the GUI aspects for it haven't been added yet for that reason).

The one area is specifically to do with handling the videos without the local setting being enabled.

The disabled setting is for setting the drive letter (it would then be set onto both the Goodies and original video location).

Aside from that, I can confirm (on this system) that the portability works for SC2K 1996, 1995 and SCURK 1996.
author: af-az

comments.body: Another possibility could be to do away with the local option entirely and have it always use the Movie directory (which would remove the use-case for setting a specific drive letter).

Yeah, I think I'd rather just have it use the MOVIES directory if present or pop up the "skipping in flight movie" dialog otherwise (if -skipvideo or the equivalent setting isn't passed). Keeps things simple and means we don't have to try to guess CD drive letters, which could easily change based on other removable drives or changes to fixed drives and their partitions.

I mean, I can think of a way to enumerate removable drives with valid filesystems and test them for presence of the SMK files but that's probably a bit much, all things considered.
In which case I'll dispense with the drive selection and the option.

title: Status dialogue will now fully redraw once it has finished being moved
body:
Disabled redraw prior to moving, re-enabled after along with an InvalidateRect() call (background erase enabled).

Similar to when you drag the main toolbar it will temporarily halt the simulation (based on tests this avoids any background actions from interrupting the dialogue movement).
author: af-az

comments.body:
Another side-effect is that while redrawing is disabled you won't see the dialogue before dragged.

If the redraw calls are disabled while InvalidateRect() is retained, the dialogue will be properly drawn but there'll be a bleed into the main game area. (Negated if the MoveWindow() Repaint flag is set to true)

This seems to just cause the status dialog to flicker rapidly on Windows 11. It sort of works on Windows 7 -- there's no window outline drawn while moving though so it's potentially a bit confusing as to where the status dialog will actually end up.

The flickering is something I encountered while writing the status dialog rendering code and it's the reason I didn't use any `InvalidateRect(hwndDlg, NULL, TRUE)` calls. Something about forcing a full repaint causes the dialog to flicker madly.

Differences between 7 and beyond..

Other experiments involved disabling redraw when you clicked down, then re-enabling (and invalidating rec) on click up, but the problem there is what happens if something interrupts the process? (such as another dialogue appearing) the click up event may be missed until you focus out and focus back into the program.

I started to dig into what was happening with the main simulation toolbar to see what the handling is in that area, though hopefully it'll be possible to do a bit more research into that over the next few days.

When dragging and dropping the simulation toolbar it appears to temporarily suspect the background simulation while still allowing for foreground graphical updates (to account for being able to see the container being dragged and also being properly updated at the end without leaving any of the bleed-effect).

More or less attempting to gather as much insight as possible in order for the front-end adjustments to be and appear as seamless as possible.

Give these latest changes a try, I've tested them under 7 and 10, and as far as I can tell from the systems here it "appears" to achieve a more desirable effect (The simulation is also paused while dragging while also retaining the border).
Looks good, works on my test platforms. Merging, thanks!
